title: In-situ S/TEM Observation of Electromechanical Strain in Antipolar and in Ion-conductive Semiconductors
content: The electromechanical coupling convers energy between electric and mechanic forms and has a wide range of useful applications. The fundamental effects behind the conversion are normally known as piezoelectricity [1] or electrostriction. While the electrostrictive effect is present in all dielectrics [2], the electrostrictive strain is typically insufficient to be used. The electromechanical coupling is also found in ionic electroactive polymers and elastomers, in which the movement of negative and positive ions under an applied local electric field generate the mechanical deformations [3]. The modern and real applications of the electroelastic effect need a large elastic strain to be established by a relatively small electric field, for which the electromechanical coupling enabled by an alternative mechanism would be highly desirable.
